clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A client receiving hemodialysis asks why infection prevention is emphasized for a central venous dialysis catheter. Which response is most accurate?

options.A: Central venous catheters have the highest infection risk among common dialysis access types, so meticulous catheter care is essential.
options.B: Dialysis catheters have lower infection risk than mature fistulas once the insertion site has healed.
options.C: Fistulas, grafts, and central venous catheters have essentially the same bloodstream-infection risk.
options.D: Catheter-related bloodstream infection is usually minor and does not justify repeated access-care precautions.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC identifies vascular-access type as a major risk factor for bloodstream infection in people receiving hemodialysis. AV fistulas have the lowest infection risk, AV grafts have an intermediate risk, and central venous catheters have the highest risk. CDC therefore emphasizes reducing catheter use when possible and applying meticulous catheter-access care, hub disinfection, aseptic technique, and patient education. Therefore option A accurately explains why infection-prevention precautions are especially important for dialysis catheters.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Recognize central venous dialysis catheters as the common hemodialysis access type with the highest bloodstream-infection risk.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest. The revised item directly tests the established dialysis-access infection-risk hierarchy without adding unnecessary claims.

option_audit.A: Correct. CDC identifies central venous catheters as the highest-risk common hemodialysis access type for infection.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Fistulas have lower infection risk than central venous catheters.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. CDC explicitly distinguishes low, intermediate, and high infection risk by access type.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Dialysis catheter bloodstream infections can be serious and warrant ongoing prevention practices.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone matches the CDC access-type infection-risk hierarchy.
cueing_check: All four choices are explanations of dialysis-access infection risk of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
